records.name: British Columbia Provincial Police Force
records.description: Established in 1871 as the British Columbia Constabulary, the provincial police came under the Attorney-General's authority at Confederation and existed until 1950.

records.name: Workmen's Compensation Board
records.description: Established 1 January 1917 under the Workmen's Compensation Act; renamed by proclamation on 1 July 1974.

records.name: Workers' Compensation Board of British Columbia
records.description: Statutory workers' compensation and workplace-safety agency, renamed from the Workmen's Compensation Board in 1974 and operating as WorkSafeBC.

records.name: Civil Service Commission
records.description: Established under the Civil Service Act of 1917 to administer testing for admission and promotion in the civil service; renamed the Public Service Commission by the Public Service Act of 1973.

records.name: Pacific Great Eastern Railway Company
records.description: Railway incorporated privately on 27 February 1912 and taken over by the provincial government in 1918 after its contractors withdrew; renamed the British Columbia Railway Company on 1 April 1972.

records.name: Game Conservation Board
records.description: Board established April 1918 to administer the Game Act; abolished in 1929 and replaced by a Game Commissioner.

records.name: Provincial Game Commissioner
records.description: Single commissioner responsible for game administration and enforcement, replaced by the Game Commission in 1934.

records.name: Game Commission
records.description: Commission established in 1934 and constituted by statute in 1935, replacing the Provincial Game Commissioner.

records.name: Public Library Commission
records.description: Created by the Public Libraries Act of 1919, administered by the Provincial Secretary, to fund and support public library associations and travelling libraries.

records.name: Liquor Control Board
records.description: Established under the Government Liquor Act of 1921, which repealed Prohibition, to run government liquor stores and issue permits; dissolved in 1973 and its functions split between the Liquor Administration Branch and the BC Liquor Board.

records.name: Liquor Distribution Branch
records.description: Government branch that took over the Liquor Control Board's store operations in 1973 (first as the Liquor Administration Branch) and now runs BC Liquor and BC Cannabis Stores.

records.name: Coal and Petroleum Control Board
records.description: Board created in 1937 to license and regulate the coal and petroleum industries; most of its mandate passed to the Public Utilities Commission in 1951 and it was disestablished in 1953.

records.name: Public Utilities Commission
records.description: Quasi-judicial regulator of utility rates and service created by the Public Utilities Act of 1938 (an earlier 1919 commission had been short-lived); terminated in 1973, with its energy functions passing to the BC Energy Commission.

records.name: Labour Relations Board
records.description: Board created under the Industrial Conciliation and Arbitration Act of 1947 to certify bargaining units and resolve disputes; made independent under the 1973 Labour Code and renamed the Industrial Relations Council in 1987.

records.name: Industrial Relations Council
records.description: Name given to the Labour Relations Board by the Industrial Relations Reform Act of 1987, reversed by the Labour Relations Code of 1992.

records.name: Labour Relations Board
records.description: Labour tribunal restored under its former name by the Labour Relations Code of 1992.

records.name: British Columbia Power Commission
records.description: Public utility created by the Hart government to electrify areas not served by BC Electric; amalgamated with the nationalized BC Electric Company on 31 March 1962 to form BC Hydro.

records.name: British Columbia Hospital Insurance Service

responsible.ministry: Dept. of Health Services and Hospital Insurance

records.description: Branch established in 1949 under the Hospital Insurance Act of 1948 to run provincial hospital insurance; renamed Hospital Programs in 1975.

records.name: British Columbia Toll Highways and Bridges Authority
records.description: Crown authority established 2 December 1953 whose ferry division began the government ferry service in 1960; renamed the British Columbia Ferry Authority on 1 April 1964.

records.name: British Columbia Ferry Authority
records.description: Crown ferry operator renamed from the Toll Highways and Bridges Authority in 1964 and renamed the British Columbia Ferry Corporation on 1 January 1977.

records.name: British Columbia Ferry Corporation
records.description: Crown corporation established under the British Columbia Ferry Corporation Act effective 1 January 1977; converted on 2 April 2003 into an independent regulated company, British Columbia Ferry Services Inc.

records.name: British Columbia Ferry Services Inc.
records.description: Former Crown corporation converted in 2003 under the Coastal Ferry Act into an independently managed, publicly owned company whose single voting share is held by the provincial B.C. Ferry Authority (not a Crown corporation).

records.name: Capital Improvement District Commission
records.description: Commission created by statute on 1 March 1956 to fund improvement and beautification projects in the Victoria capital region; became the Provincial Capital Commission in 1977.

records.name: British Columbia Electric Company (provincially owned)
records.description: The private BC Electric utility, expropriated by the provincial government on 1 August 1961 and merged with the BC Power Commission in 1962 to form BC Hydro.

records.name: British Columbia Hydro and Power Authority
records.description: Provincial electric utility formed by merging the nationalized BC Electric Company with the BC Power Commission; it shed its gas and transit operations from 1979 and re-absorbed BC Transmission Corporation in 2010.

records.name: British Columbia Housing Management Commission
records.description: Constituted a body corporate by order in council approved 8 December 1967 to develop, administer and manage social housing; known as BC Housing.

records.name: Mediation Commission
records.description: Commission established under the Mediation Commission Act to mediate labour disputes; its functions passed to the Department of Labour's Mediation Services Branch in 1972.

records.name: British Columbia Railway Company
records.description: Renamed from the Pacific Great Eastern Railway in 1972 and operated as BC Rail from 1984; its freight operations were leased to CN in 2004, and it continues to hold railway and port lands as a subsidiary of the BC Transportation Financing Authority.

records.name: British Columbia Development Corporation
records.description: Crown corporation established 31 March 1973 to assist industrial enterprises; merged into the new British Columbia Enterprise Corporation effective 31 March 1987.

records.name: British Columbia Energy Commission
records.description: Established under the Energy Act of 1973 to take over the energy functions of the Public Utilities Commission; replaced by the British Columbia Utilities Commission in 1980.

records.name: Insurance Corporation of British Columbia
records.description: Crown corporation created in 1973 by the Barrett government to administer compulsory public auto insurance (Autoplan) and later driver and vehicle licensing.

records.name: British Columbia Land Commission
records.description: Created by the Land Commission Act, proclaimed 18 May 1973, which also established the Agricultural Land Reserve.

records.name: Provincial Agricultural Land Commission
records.description: The Land Commission renamed under the Agricultural Land Commission Act of January 1978; it administers the Agricultural Land Reserve.

records.name: Ocean Falls Corporation
records.description: Formed in 1973 when the province bought the town of Ocean Falls and its pulp mill from Crown Zellerbach; the mill closed in 1980 and the corporation was dissolved in 1986.

records.name: British Columbia Petroleum Corporation
records.description: Crown corporation created by the Petroleum Corporation Act (assented 7 November 1973) to buy and sell natural gas and petroleum; partially privatized in 1990 and dissolved in September 1994, its functions absorbed by the Ministry of Energy, Mines and Petroleum Resources.

records.name: Human Rights Commission
records.description: Established by the Human Rights Code of British Columbia Act of 1973; replaced by the BC Council of Human Rights in 1984.

records.name: British Columbia Assessment Authority
records.description: Independent Crown corporation that values all real property in the province, created by the Assessment Authority Act (Royal Assent 2 July 1974).

records.name: Emergency Health Services Commission
records.description: Commission created by legislation in 1974 to provide a provincial ambulance service (BC Ambulance Service) and medical disaster planning; became BC Emergency Health Services, a PHSA division, in 2013.

records.name: Legal Services Commission
records.description: Commission established August 1975, replacing the Legal Services Division; amalgamated with the Legal Aid Society of B.C. on 1 October 1979 to form the Legal Services Society.

records.name: British Columbia Steamship Company (1975) Ltd.
records.description: Crown corporation created in 1975 to restore Victoria-Seattle passenger and car service with the Princess Marguerite, bought from Canadian Pacific; dissolved in 1992.

records.name: British Columbia Buildings Corporation
records.description: Crown corporation that served as the government's landlord (over 3,400 buildings by 1994), established 30 June 1976 and dissolved in 2006 under the Public Agency Accommodation Act.

records.name: British Columbia Systems Corporation
records.description: Crown corporation created under the System Act on 1 September 1977 to provide data-processing and telecommunications services to ministries; broken up in 1996.

records.name: British Columbia Resources Investment Corporation
records.description: Holding company for Crown-owned mills and mines bought in 1972-75, known for the free 'Brick' shares of 1979; renamed Westar Group Ltd. and made a publicly traded company, no longer a Crown corporation, by a 1988 amendment.

records.name: British Columbia Heritage Trust
records.description: Crown corporation established under the Heritage Conservation Act of 1977 to fund heritage conservation; its operations were terminated on 31 March 2003 after the Core Services Review.

records.name: Provincial Capital Commission
records.description: Crown agency (successor to the Capital Improvement District Commission) that stewarded capital-region heritage properties such as the Crystal Garden and St. Ann's Academy; its elimination was announced in November 2013 and it was dissolved in 2014.

records.name: BC Games Society
records.description: Crown corporation created in 1977 to run the BC Summer and Winter Games and manage Team BC at the Canada Games.

records.name: Open Learning Institute
records.description: Distance-education institute created in 1978 under the BC Colleges and Provincial Institutes Act; combined with the Knowledge Network into the Open Learning Agency in 1988.

records.name: Science Council of British Columbia
records.description: Crown agency created in 1978 under the Science Council Act to promote science and technology; its Act was retitled the Innovation and Science Council Act in 2003 and it became the BC Innovation Council in 2004.

records.name: British Columbia Film Commission
records.description: Provincial film-promotion office founded in 1978 under Tourism Minister Grace McCarthy; merged with BC Film + Media in April 2013 to form Creative BC.

records.name: Expo 86 Corporation
records.description: Provincial nonprofit agency, set up under the Transpo 86 Corporation Act of 1980, that planned and ran the Expo 86 world's fair (2 May-13 October 1986), headed by Jim Pattison.

records.name: Urban Transit Authority
records.description: Crown corporation created in 1979 to coordinate planning, marketing and funding of municipal transit; took over Victoria and Vancouver transit from BC Hydro in 1980 and was renamed BC Transit in 1982.

records.name: Metro Transit Operating Company
records.description: Crown corporation established by the Metro Transit Operating Company Act to operate Vancouver-area transit; merged with the Urban Transit Authority into BC Transit.

records.name: Legal Services Society
records.description: Statutory legal-aid provider formed on 1 October 1979 by amalgamating the Legal Services Commission and the Legal Aid Society of B.C.; it now operates as Legal Aid BC.

records.name: British Columbia Place Ltd.
records.description: Crown corporation established May 1980 (developer of BC Place); renamed British Columbia Enterprise Corporation in March 1987.

records.name: BC Transit
records.description: Provincial transit Crown corporation, renamed from the Urban Transit Authority in 1982; it handed Metro Vancouver transit to TransLink in 1999 and now coordinates transit elsewhere in the province.

records.name: British Columbia Utilities Commission
records.description: Independent regulator of energy utilities, pipelines and ICBC basic insurance rates, established by the Utilities Commission Act in 1980.

records.name: W.L.C. Developments Ltd.
records.description: Crown-owned company established January 1983 to develop and sell Crown land in Whistler; its mandate was broadened in 1997 and it was renamed in 1998.

records.name: B.C. Pavilion Corporation
records.description: Crown corporation incorporated in 1984 under the Company Act that took over BC Enterprise Corporation's remaining assets in 1989 and operates BC Place and the Vancouver Convention Centre.

records.name: British Columbia Lottery Corporation
records.description: Crown corporation incorporated 25 October 1984 that began selling lottery tickets in 1985 after B.C. left the Western Canada Lottery Foundation; it now also runs casino and online gambling.

records.name: BC Council of Human Rights
records.description: Body that replaced the Human Rights Commission in 1984; replaced in 1997 by a new Human Rights Commission, Advisory Council and Tribunal.

records.name: British Columbia Enterprise Corporation
records.description: Crown corporation formed in March 1987 by renaming BC Place Ltd. and merging in the BC Development Corporation; it ceased operations on 30 September 1989, transferring its assets to the Province and B.C. Pavilion Corporation.

records.name: Open Learning Agency
records.description: Crown agency established by legislation early in 1988, combining the Knowledge Network with the Open Learning Institute; its university function moved to Thompson Rivers University in 2005 and it was continued as the Knowledge Network Corporation in 2007.

records.name: Financial Institutions Commission
records.description: Regulator of credit unions, insurance and trust companies, pension plans and mortgage brokers from 1989 until it was replaced by the BC Financial Services Authority in 2019.

records.name: First Peoples' Cultural Council
records.description: First Nations-governed Crown corporation established in 1990 under the First Peoples' Heritage, Language and Culture Act to support Indigenous language, arts and culture.

records.name: British Columbia Treaty Commission
records.description: Independent body co-established in 1992 by Canada, British Columbia and the First Nations Summit to facilitate treaty negotiations, later given provincial and federal statutory footing.

records.name: BC Transportation Financing Authority
records.description: Crown corporation established in 1993 under the Transportation Act to plan, acquire, build and hold transportation infrastructure.

records.name: Columbia Power Corporation
records.description: Crown corporation created in 1994 to buy hydroelectric rights from Cominco, later developing Columbia Basin power projects with the Columbia Basin Trust.

records.name: Forest Renewal BC
records.description: Crown corporation created under the Forest Renewal Act of 1994 to reinvest stumpage revenue in forests and forest communities; the Act was repealed effective 27 June 2002 and a forest investment account replaced it.

records.name: Forest Practices Board
records.description: Independent watchdog for forest and range practices, established under the Forest Practices Code of British Columbia Act of 1994 (code proclaimed 15 June 1995).

records.name: Columbia Basin Trust
records.description: Regional trust created by the Columbia Basin Trust Act in 1995 to benefit the region most affected by the Columbia River Treaty.

records.name: British Columbia Securities Commission
records.description: Self-funded Crown corporation created on 1 April 1995 to administer the Securities Act and regulate capital markets.

records.name: British Columbia Arts Council
records.description: Statutory agency created by the BC Arts Council Act of 1995 to fund the arts.

records.name: Tourism British Columbia
records.description: Crown corporation established in 1997 to market the province to tourists; merged into the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and the Arts on 1 April 2010.

records.name: BC Human Rights Commission
records.description: Commission created by the Human Rights Amendment Act of 1995 to investigate complaints alongside the new Tribunal; abolished by the Campbell government in 2003.

records.name: BC Human Rights Tribunal
records.description: Adjudicative body under the Human Rights Code, created by the Human Rights Amendment Act of 1995 and hearing cases since 1997; took over complaint screening when the Commission was abolished in 2003.

records.name: Regional health boards, community health councils and community health services societies
records.description: Under the 1997 amendments to the Health Authorities Act, 52 local health authorities (11 regional health boards, 34 community health councils, 7 community health services societies) ran health services until they were amalgamated into five regional authorities in December 2001.

records.name: Industry Training and Apprenticeship Commission
records.description: Arm's-length commission of business, labour, education and government, announced 23 June 1997 to govern industry training and apprenticeship; dissolved in 2003.

records.name: British Columbia Assets and Land Corporation
records.description: Renamed from W.L.C. Developments in 1998 to sell surplus Crown land and administer Crown land tenures; renamed Land and Water British Columbia Inc. in 2002.

records.name: Greater Vancouver Transportation Authority
records.description: Statutory regional transportation authority created in 1998 and fully in operation in April 1999, replacing BC Transit in Greater Vancouver.

records.name: BC Oil and Gas Commission
records.description: Crown regulator of oil and gas activities and pipelines, established in October 1998 under the Oil and Gas Commission Act.

records.name: British Columbia Investment Management Corporation
records.description: Investment manager for public-sector pension plans, created by the Public Sector Pension Plans Act of 1999 to take over assets managed by the Ministry of Finance.

records.name: British Columbia Pension Corporation
records.description: Pension administration agent for the College, Municipal, Public Service, Teachers' and WorkSafeBC plans, created in 2000 under the Public Sector Pension Plans Act.

records.name: Merit Commissioner
records.description: Office created in 2001 (an independent officer of the Legislature from 2005) to audit merit-based public-service hiring; dissolved by the Budget Measures Implementation Act, 2026, with the role transferred to the head of the BC Public Service Agency.

records.name: Fraser Health Authority
records.description: One of five regional health authorities created by the December 2001 amalgamation under the Regional Health Boards Regulation (B.C. Reg. 293/2001). Amalgamated the Fraser Valley, Simon Fraser and South Fraser health regions.

records.name: Interior Health Authority
records.description: One of five regional health authorities created by the December 2001 amalgamation under the Regional Health Boards Regulation (B.C. Reg. 293/2001). Amalgamated about 20 former health regions and councils in the southern Interior.

records.name: Northern Health Authority
records.description: One of five regional health authorities created by the December 2001 amalgamation under the Regional Health Boards Regulation (B.C. Reg. 293/2001). Amalgamated the Northern Interior Regional Health Board and northern health councils.

records.name: Vancouver Coastal Health Authority
records.description: One of five regional health authorities created by the December 2001 amalgamation under the Regional Health Boards Regulation (B.C. Reg. 293/2001). Amalgamated the Vancouver/Richmond Health Board, North Shore Health Region and coastal community health councils.

records.name: Vancouver Island Health Authority
records.description: One of five regional health authorities created by the December 2001 amalgamation under the Regional Health Boards Regulation (B.C. Reg. 293/2001). Amalgamated the Capital Health Region, Central Vancouver Island Health Region and island health councils.

records.name: Provincial Health Services Authority
records.description: Province-wide health authority created in December 2001 to run specialized provincial services such as BC Cancer, BCCDC and BC Emergency Health Services; its mandate was refocused after a 2025 review.

records.name: Partnerships British Columbia
records.description: Crown corporation created in 2002 to plan and procure public-private partnership infrastructure projects; began operating as Infrastructure BC in January 2021.

records.name: Land and Water British Columbia Inc.
records.description: BCAL renamed in 2002 with an expanded mandate over water licensing and allocation as well as Crown land; eliminated in the 2005 government reorganization.

records.name: British Columbia Transmission Corporation
records.description: Crown corporation formed under the Transmission Corporation Act of 2003 to operate BC Hydro's transmission system independently; re-merged into BC Hydro in 2010 under the Clean Energy Act.

records.name: Royal British Columbia Museum
records.description: Provincial museum founded in 1886, styled 'Royal' from 1987, which merged with the BC Provincial Archives in 2003 and is listed as a provincial Crown corporation.

records.name: Industry Training Authority
records.description: Agency established in 2004 to replace ITAC after mandatory trades certification was abolished in 2003; renamed SkilledTradesBC in December 2022.

records.name: BC Innovation Council
records.description: Crown agency formed in 2004 by merging the Advanced Science Institute BC (as Wikipedia styles it) and the Innovation and Science Council of British Columbia; renamed Innovate BC in 2018.

records.name: BC Safety Authority
records.description: Independent technical-safety regulator since 2004; adopted the operating name Technical Safety BC on 20 September 2017.

records.name: Northern Development Initiative Trust
records.description: Regional economic-development trust for central and northern B.C., created by the Northern Development Initiative Trust Act (Bill 59, introduced 6 October 2004) with proceeds from the BC Rail deal.

records.name: Community Living British Columbia
records.description: Crown agency under the Community Living Authority Act, incorporated 1 July 2005, providing supports for adults with developmental disabilities.

records.name: Island Coastal Economic Trust
records.description: One of three provincially funded regional economic trusts, created in 2006 for Vancouver Island and the coast.

records.name: Knowledge Network Corporation
records.description: The Open Learning Agency continued under the Knowledge Network Corporation Act (assented 31 May 2007) as the Crown owner of the public educational broadcaster, on air since 12 January 1981.

records.name: South Coast British Columbia Transportation Authority
records.description: TransLink's official name after legislation approved 29 November 2007 changed the authority's governance and name; it runs Metro Vancouver's regional transit, major roads and bridges.

records.name: Pacific Carbon Trust
records.description: Crown carbon-offset agency established in 2008; its elimination was announced on 19 November 2013 and its offset program was moved into the Environment Ministry.

records.name: Transportation Investment Corporation
records.description: Crown corporation established in 2008 under the Transportation Investment Act to deliver the Port Mann/Highway 1 project, later other major transportation projects.

records.name: Destination BC Corp.
records.description: Crown corporation created under the Business Corporations Act on 2 November 2012 (operating from 1 April 2013) to market B.C. tourism, reversing the 2010 absorption of Tourism BC into government.

records.name: Creative BC
records.description: Agency formed in April 2013 by merging the BC Film Commission and BC Film + Media to develop the province's creative industries.

records.name: BC Emergency Health Services
records.description: The Emergency and Health Services Commission renamed and made a division of PHSA in 2013; it runs BC Ambulance Service.

records.name: Technical Safety BC
records.description: Operating name adopted by the BC Safety Authority on 20 September 2017.

records.name: Innovate BC
records.description: Crown agency funding technology start-up and commercialization programs, renamed from the BC Innovation Council in 2018.

records.name: BC Financial Services Authority
records.description: Crown agency that replaced FICOM in November 2019 and on 1 August 2021 absorbed the Real Estate Council of BC and the Superintendent of Real Estate's office.

records.name: Infrastructure BC
records.description: Operating name, adopted in January 2021, of the Crown corporation formerly Partnerships BC, with an expanded project-procurement mandate.

records.name: InBC Investment Corp.
records.description: Crown corporation set up in 2021 as the Province's $500-million strategic investment fund; its board was appointed on 6 May 2021.

records.name: SkilledTradesBC
records.description: The Industry Training Authority renamed in December 2022 as the government reintroduced mandatory skilled-trades certification.

records.name: British Columbia Energy Regulator
records.description: The Oil and Gas Commission renamed under the Energy Statutes Amendment Act, 2022 (name change announced February 2023), with a mandate expanded to hydrogen, methanol and ammonia.

records.name: BC Shared Health Services
records.description: Standalone shared-services organization, announced in December 2025 after the health-authority review and formally established on 1 April 2026 within the Health Employers Association of BC, to centralize corporate and administrative services for all health authorities.

gaps: Merit Commissioner: Budget Measures Implementation Act, 2026 brings the dissolution (ss. 13-27) into force by regulation; the exact in-force date was not found, so 'ended' is given as 2026 (commissioner's term ended 10 March 2026, acting commissioner appointed for the transition).

BC Oil and Gas Commission -> BC Energy Regulator: exact in-force date of the renaming not found; Act received Royal Assent 24 Nov 2022, and the official name change was announced 17 Feb 2023 (recorded as 2023).

Liquor Distribution Branch: BC Archives says the Liquor Control Board's store functions went to a 'Liquor Administration Branch' in 1973; when that name became 'Liquor Distribution Branch' was not found.

BC Transit start date: BC Transit and BC Archives say the UTA was renamed BC Transit in 1982; Wikipedia says BC Transit was created in 1983 by merging the UTA and MTOC. MTOC's end is given as 1983 from Wikipedia.
BC Hydro: BC Archives dates it to the 31 March 1962 amalgamation; Wikipedia says 'created in 1961' (the BC Electric expropriation of 1 August 1961 is recorded as a separate record).
Pacific Carbon Trust: elimination announced 19 Nov 2013; the actual wind-up date was not found (ended recorded as 2013).
Land and Water BC: eliminated in the June 2005 reorganization per an undated Dogwood article; exact date not found.
Provincial Capital Commission: dissolution year 2014 comes from Wikipedia; the elimination was announced in November 2013.
Legal Services Society began operating as Legal Aid BC around 2020 (the announcement page is undated), so this is kept as one record with shortName, not a rename record.

Not included because no reliable start or end date was found: Environmental Assessment Office (Wikipedia says 2002, but the Environmental Assessment Act was proclaimed in 1995), Law Reform Commission of BC (est. 1 July 1969, end not found), Alcohol and Drug Commission (est. 5 June 1973, end not found), BC Harbours Board (est. 1967, end not found), Land Settlement Board (est. 1917), BC Housing Corporation, Dunhill Development Corporation, Southern Interior Development Initiative Trust (2006 only from a ZoomInfo summary), BC Cancer Agency, Western Canada Lottery Foundation (interprovincial), B.C. Ferry Authority (2003), Vancouver Wharves, BC Rail Ltd. (1984 operating subsidiary), BC Film + Media, Crown agencies such as BC Council for International Education, BC Family Maintenance Agency, Forest Enhancement Society, Forestry Innovation Investment and BC Infrastructure Benefits (all on the 2026 gov.bc.ca Crown list), and Okanagan-specific provincial bodies (none confirmed).
First Nations Health Authority was left out: it is a tripartite First Nations organization, not a provincial body (federal programs transferred 1 October 2013).

Responsible-ministry periods are included only where a source states them (Hospital Insurance Service, Game Commissioner, Provincial Police, LDB since 2025); gov.bc.ca pages give each current Crown corporation's ministry but no start year, so those are not recorded.
Expo 86 Corporation: BC Archives gives 1979-1986 for dates of existence; Wikipedia gives the Transpo 86 Corporation Act (1980) and says Expo 86 Corporation was 'established' by the end of 1981.
